claim.quote: the lifetime reported here (877.7 $\pm$ 0.7 (stat) +0.4/-0.2 (sys) s) is the first modern measurement of $\tau_n$ that does not require corrections larger than the quoted uncertainties.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Science 360, 627 (2018).

name: Measurement of the neutron lifetime using an asymmetric magneto-gravitational trap and in situ detection

summary.plain: UCNtau held ultracold neutrons above a magnetic surface so that they never touch a wall and measured their lifetime as 877.7 seconds, the first modern storage measurement that needs no correction larger than its uncertainty.
summary.technical: Polarized UCN levitated in an asymmetric magneto-gravitational trap with in situ detection: tau_n = 877.7 ± 0.7 stat +0.4/-0.2 syst s; the beam (887.7 ± 2.2 s) and bottle (878.5 ± 0.8 s) results differed by 3.9 sigma when the paper was written.

title: Measurement of the neutron lifetime using an asymmetric magneto-gravitational trap and in situ detection
why_it_matters: The abstract frames the result against a 3.9 standard deviation discrepancy between the beam and material-trap storage results.
